subject: History
sourceFile: Copy of History BECE Syllabus - syllabusNG.txt
examFormat: History was added to the Basic Education Curriculum to give students a body of knowledge for understanding history as a tool for forging national identity, national integration, patriotism and unity, and for understanding similarities and differences among Nigerian peoples. The exam has two compulsory papers of 60 multiple-choice questions each, 1 hour each, one mark per question; the 120 questions make up 70% and the school's Continuous Assessment 30%. Paper 1: Concept of History (20 questions), Geography and Environment (20) and Geographical Environment (20). Paper 2: Political Development in Nigeria (40) and External Contact and Trade (20).
excluded: syllabus.ng 'About us', 'About BECE', eligibility, grading, registration and FAQ chapters. Obvious extraction typos fixed (e.g. 'Bomo' → 'Borno', 'Kano-Feuan' → 'Kano-Fezzan', 'Kanuri Born of Hausa States' read as 'Kanuri Borno/Hausa States', 'alm oil' → 'palm oil'). The effect 'Introduction of international' was cut off in the text and is given as 'international trade'.
recommendedTexts: History for Secondary Schools in Nigeria, J.S.S. 1-3 — Historical Society of Nigeria (HSN) (Journal of the Historical Society of Nigeria vol. 1, 2 and 3)
Minds Exploits History Studies for Junior Secondary Schools, Books 1-3 — Babajide Amao and Joseph Adetunji (Mind Exploits Publishers)
History for Junior Secondary Schools — Nnaemeka Uwakwe Itiri (Nigerian Defence Academy Publishers)

topics.name: Meaning of History
objectives: Explain the meaning of History
Distinguish between History and storytelling (e.g. History is time-based and factual)

topics.name: Sources of History
objectives: Explain the meaning of sources of History
Identify primary, secondary and tertiary sources of History
Describe how to access sources of History

subtopics.name: Primary sources of History
objectives: Identify primary sources: oral traditions, artifacts, legends, folklores, archival materials, etc.

subtopics.name: Secondary sources of History
objectives: Identify secondary sources: textbooks, journals, articles, government publications, biographies, autobiographies, etc.

subtopics.name: Tertiary sources of History
objectives: Identify tertiary sources: students' projects, bulletins, memoranda (memos), etc.

subtopics.name: How to access sources of History
objectives: Describe ways of accessing sources: excursions to historical sites, exhibitions, libraries, cultural festivals, museums, etc.

topics.name: Importance of History
objectives: State the importance of History to the individual, society and the nation

topics.name: Major Centralized States in Pre-Colonial Nigeria
objectives: Explain the meaning of centralized states
State the characteristics of centralized states
Give examples of centralized states in pre-colonial Nigeria
topics.content: Theme: Political Developments in Nigeria. Examples of centralized states in pre-colonial Nigeria: Hausa States, Kanem Borno, Nupe Kingdom, Oyo Empire, Igala Kingdom, Benin Empire, Niger Delta City States, Calabar.

topics.name: Non-centralized States in Pre-Colonial Nigeria
objectives: Explain the meaning of non-centralized states
State the characteristics of non-centralized states
Give examples of non-centralized states in pre-colonial Nigeria
topics.content: Theme: Political Developments in Nigeria. Examples of non-centralized states in pre-colonial Nigeria: Tiv, Idoma, Ebira, Igbo, Urhobo, Ijo (Ijaw), Ibibio, Anang, Oro (Oron).

topics.name: Interrelationships of some Centres of Civilization in Pre-colonial Nigeria
objectives: Describe the relationships between people from different centres of civilization in pre-colonial Nigeria (e.g. Ife/Benin, Kanuri Borno/Hausa States, Igbo/Niger Delta City States)
State the differences that existed between different centres of civilization in pre-colonial Nigeria: political structure, culture and customs, religious beliefs, etc.
Identify areas of interaction among people of centres of civilization in pre-colonial Nigeria: trade and commerce, marriage, festivals, wars, etc.

topics.name: Origin and Organization of Trans-Saharan Trade
objectives: Explain the origin and nature of the Trans-Saharan Trade

subtopics.name: Commodities traded during Trans-Saharan Trade
objectives: Identify the commodities traded: gold, salt, horses, slaves, ostrich feathers, spices, etc.

subtopics.name: Trade routes during Trans-Saharan Trade
objectives: Identify the trade routes: Borno-Tripoli route, Kanem Borno-Sudan route, Kano-Fezzan route

subtopics.name: Effects of Trans-Saharan Trade
objectives: State the effects: introduction of international trade, use of camels as a means of transportation, slave trade across the Sahara, Islam and the Arabic language; encouraged interaction between North Africa and West Africa, etc.

objectives: Describe the nature of early European contacts with Nigeria

subtopics.name: Trans-Atlantic Slave Trade

subtopics.name: Legitimate trade (palm oil)

topics.name: British Colonization of Nigerian Territories

topics.name: The Evolution of the Nigerian State
objectives: State the major reasons for, and major features of, the Berlin Treaty
Explain the roles of the Royal Niger Company in Nigerian territories
Describe the colonial conquest and administration of Nigerian territories

topics.name: The Amalgamation of Nigeria
objectives: Explain the meaning of amalgamation
State the reasons for the amalgamation of Nigerian territories
Describe the process of the amalgamation of Nigerian territories
Identify key personalities and their roles in the amalgamation: Taubman Goldie, Lord Lugard, the European missionaries, Nigerian traditional rulers, etc.

topics.name: The Independence Movement
objectives: Explain the meaning of nationalism
State the factors that contributed to Nigerian nationalism
Describe the nature of Nigerian nationalism: the struggle for independence and the people involved in it
Describe the attainment of independence in 1960
